Hi all — thanks Naomi. Quick legal checklist and asks from our side so Acme knows what to expect before we execute: 

- We will execute EU SCCs + UK IDTA jointly; standard practice is DocuSign signature block for both.
- Please confirm the scope of the data categories (PII, health data, derived embeddings) — if health data is included, we will require the TIA plus the subprocessor matrix.
- Evidence we can provide immediately: SOC 2 report (redacted), encryption-at-rest + in-transit statements, KMS key custody summary, list of active subprocessors and their processing regions.
- If Acme requires HSM-backed key custody or a dedicated residency guarantee, that will be a follow-on procurement conversation.

I reviewed Acme's redlines quickly and flagged three items that typically require negotiation:
1) Broad liability cap increases — we usually counter.
2) Data localization carve-outs in Section 7 — need to confirm technical feasibility.
3) Deletion/retention strictures requiring wholesale log deletion on short notice — we need a runbook.

Next steps from Redwood Legal: I will prepare a one-page deviation memo and upload redlines_marked.docx to the Drive folder by 18:00 ET today. If Acme can accept the deviations or propose compromises, we can issue the DocuSign packet tomorrow.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
